questions.q_en: In a race of 2000 m, Ajay beats Ansh by 220 m. If the speed of Ajay is 36 km/h, then the speed of Ansh is:
questions.solution_en:
Ajay beats Ansh by 220 m in a 2000 m race, which means Ansh runs 1780 m in the time Ajay runs 2000 m.

So, we can find Ansh's speed by proportionality.

The speed of Ansh = (2000 - 220) * 36/2000

= 32.04 km/h

questions.q_en: In an 8 km race, P gave a 2000 m head start to Q. If they finished the race at the same time and the speed of Q is 14.4 km/h, the speed of P is?
questions.solution_en:
When P moves 8 km, then Q moves = 8 - 2000/1000 = 6 km

Time taken by Q to move 6 km = 6/14.4 = 6 * 60/14.4 = 25 minutes

Speed of P = 8/ (25/60) = 19.2 km/h

questions.q_en: In a 480 m race, Pritam runs at a speed of 32 m/sec. He gives a start of 40 m to Aruna and still defeats him by 1 second. The speed of Aruna is?
questions.solution_en:
Time taken by Pritam to cover 480 m = 480/32 = 15 seconds

Distance covered by Aruna = 480 - 40 = 440 m

Time taken by Aruna = 15 + 1 = 16 seconds

Hence, the speed of Aruna = 440/16 = 27.5 m/s

questions.q_en: In a 750 m race, X runs at 15 km/h. X gives Y a head start of 30 m and still beats him by 60 seconds. Find the speed of X.
questions.solution_en:
[To convert km/h in m/s, multiply with 5/18]

15 km/h = 75/18 m/s

Time taken by X to cover 750 m = 750/(75/18) = 180 seconds

Distance covered by Y = 750 - 30 = 720 m

Time taken by Y to cover 720 m = 180 + 60 = 240 seconds

Hence, the speed of Y = 720/ 240 = 3 m/s = 3 * 18/5 = 10.8 km/h

questions.q_en: Nita gives Nidhi a head start of 20 m in a race of 600 m. Nita runs at the speed of 18 km/h. If Nita managed to beat Nidhi by 25 seconds, find the ratio of speeds of Nita and Nidhi if they started the race at the same time.
questions.solution_en:
[To convert km/h in m/s, multiply with 5/18]

18 km/h = 5 m/sec

Time taken by Nita to cover 600 m = 600/5 = 120 seconds

Distance covered by Nidhi = 600 - 20 = 580 m

Time taken by Nidhi to cover 580 m = 120 + 25 = 145 seconds

The speed of Nishi = 580/145 = 4 m/sec

Hence, the required ratio = 5 /4 = 5 : 4

questions.q_en: In a linear race of 780 m, A beats B by 60 m or 5 seconds. What is the difference between A and B speeds (in m/s)?
questions.solution_en:
When A covers 780 m B covers 720 m

Also, B covers 60 m in 5 seconds

So, the speed of B = 60/5 = 12 m/sec

Time taken by B to cover 720 m = 720/ 12 = 60 seconds

Speed of A = 780/60 = 13 m/s

Hence, the difference between the speed of A and B = 13 - 12 = 1 m/s

questions.q_en: In a linear race of 900 m, A beats B by 80 m or 8 seconds. What is the difference between A and B speeds (in m/s)?
questions.solution_en:
When A covers 900 m B covers 820 m

Also, B covers 80 m in 8 seconds

questions.q_en: In a 1500 m race, bike A beats bike B by 300 m. bike B beats bike C by 200 m in a 900 m race. If bike A beats bike C by 30 seconds in a 1350 m race, then what is the speed of bike C?

When bike A covers 1500 m bike B covers 1200 m

The ratio of speed = 5: 4

When bike B covers 900 m bike C covers 700 m

The ratio of speed = 9: 7

The ratio of A, B, and C = 45 : 36: 28

When bike A covers 1350 m, C covers = 1350 * 28/45 = 840 m

So, difference = 1350 - 840 = 510

Bike C will cover the remaining 510 m in 30 seconds

Hence, the speed of bike C = 510/30 = 17 m/sec

questions.q_en: Gita runs 5/3 times as fast as Bablu. In a race, if Gita gives a lead of 35 m to Bablu, find the distance from the starting point where both will meet.
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of Bablu be '3x'

The speed of Gita = 5x

Let the distance covered by Gita be 'y' meters

The distance covered by Bablu = y - 35 meters

As time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed

3x/5x = (y - 35)/y

3y = 5y - 175

2y = 175

y = 87.5

The distance from the starting point where both will meet is 87.5 m.

questions.q_en: A runs 25% faster than B and can allow B a lead of 12 meters to end a race in a dead heat. What is the length of the race?
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of B be '100'

The speed of A = 100 * 25/100 = 125

The ratio of speed of A to B = 125/100 = 5: 4

Therefore, the ratio of distance covered by them will also be 5: 4

(5 - 4)unit = 12

1unit = 12

5 unit= 60

Hence, the length of the race = 60 meters

questions.q_en: A takes 5 minutes and 40 seconds while B takes 6 minutes to complete a race. A beat B by 90 meters in the race if both start simultaneously from the starting point. Find the length of the course.
questions.solution_en:
Time taken by A = 5 * 60 + 40 = 340 seconds

Time taken by B = 6 * 60 = 360 seconds

B cover distance in 20 seconds = 90

B cover distance in 360 seconds = 360 * 90/20

= 1620 meters

Hence, the length of the course = 1620 meters

questions.q_en: Three runners Ritu, Rupesh, and Rishu run a race, with Ritu finishing 60 metres ahead of Rupesh and 90 m ahead of Rishu. In another race of the same length, Rupesh finished 35 meters ahead of Rishu. Each runner travels the entire distance at a constant speed. Find the length of the race.
questions.solution_en:
Let the length of the race be 'D' meters

When Ritu traveled a distance of D meters, then Rupesh traveled (D - 60) meters and Rishu traveled (D - 90) meters

When Rupesh traveled D meters, then Rishu traveled (D - 35) meters

Comparing both scenarios of Rupesh and Rishu

(D - 60)/ (D - 90) = D/(D - 35)

D2 - 35D - 60D + 2100 = D2 - 90D

5D = 2100

D = 420 meters

questions.q_en: A and B run a race of 4 km. First, A gives B a head start of 400 m and beats him by 60 seconds. While coming back, A gives B a lead of 2 minutes 40 seconds and gets beaten by 800 m. What is the difference between the times in minutes in which A and B can run the race for one side separately?
questions.solution_en:
When A covers 4000 m, then B covers 3600 meters

Let the speed of A and B be 'x' m/ minutes and 'y' m/minutes

3600/y - 4000/x = 60/60

3600/y - 4000/x = 1 .... (i)

When A covers 3200 m, then B covers 4000 meters

2 minutes 40 seconds = 8/3 minutes

4000/y - 3200/x = 8/3 .... (ii)

Multiply (ii) by 5/4

5000/y - 4000/x = 10/3 ... (iii)

From (i) and (iii)

1400/y = 7/3

y = 600 m/minutes

Time taken by B to cover 4000 m = 4000/600 = 20/3 minutes

3600/600 - 4000/x = 1

6 - 4000/x = 1

x = 4000/5 = 800 m/minutes

Time taken by A to cover 4000 m = 4000/800 = 5 minutes

Hence, the required difference = 20/3 - 5 = 5/3 minutes

questions.q_en: A and B run a race of 3 km. First, A gives B a head start of 600 m and beats him by 120 seconds. While coming back, A gives B a lead of 5 minutes and gets beaten by 500 m. What is the difference between the times in minutes in which A and B can run the race for one side separately?
questions.solution_en:
When A covers 3000 m, then B covers 2400 meters

Let the speed of A and B be 'x' m/ minutes and 'y' m/minutes

2400/y - 3000/x = 120/60

2400/y - 3000/x = 2 .... (i)

When A covers 2500 m, then B covers 3000 meters

3000/y - 2500/x = 5 .... (ii)

Multiply (ii) by 6/5

3600/y - 3000/x = 6 ... (iii)

From (i) and (iii)

1200/y = 4

y = 300 m/minutes

Time taken by B to cover 3000 m = 3000/300 = 10 minutes

2400/300 - 3000/x = 2

8 - 3000/x = 2

x = 3000/6 = 500 m/minutes

Time taken by A to cover 3000 m = 3000/500 = 6 minutes

Hence, the required difference = 10 - 6 = 4 minutes
